The man had heard that Chase was the guy building a new data center in town—and he wanted to say: Please don’t. “He had a beautiful home that he paid for and had been living in for years, and was concerned that his view would be disrupted,” Chase told me. articles.title: New York Republicans Are Ripping Each Other to Shreds
articles.author: Holly Pretsky
articles.summary: New York City's Republican of the Moment Curtis Sliwa is DEFINITELY NOT demoralized by the absolute shellacking his party got on Tuesday. "I view this complete tsunami, this blue tsunami, especially when it relates to the 62 counties of New York, as Liberation Day for Republicans who no longer feel that if they're not MAGA, they don't exist," Sliwa told Hell Gate. "You know, 'We're RINOs.' Well, guess what? I'm a proud RINO." (In case you've never seen Fox News, that's a Trumpworld pejorative that stands for "Republican In Name Only.") The losses went far beyond GOP candidate Bruce Blakeman's double-digit defeat by Governor Kathy Hochul. Republicans lost at least six state Senate seats, at least seven Assembly seats, a major congressional seat in the Hudson Valley, all three statewide races by double-digit margins, and they barely hung onto a seat in the deep red North Country with a pretty embarrassing candidate . Still, Sliwa's feeling…optimistic. "This is a perfect opportunity for Republicans to organize and mobilize. The people united will never be defeated," he said.
